paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage hands you. A king puts himself above every god, and he is successful for a while. But the text says it's only "until the time of wrath is completed, for what has been decreed must be accomplished" (Daniel 11:36). He looks like the biggest thing in the room, and he still isn't the one holding the clock.

Then comes the part that's for you. In the middle of a time of distress, God's people are delivered, "everyone whose name is found written in the book" (Daniel 12:1). Many who sleep in the dust will awake, some to everlasting life, and "those who lead many to righteousness will shine like the stars forever and ever" (Daniel 12:2-3). So the way you live now isn't wasted, because it matters all the way to the end.

Now, Daniel himself heard and did not understand, and he was told to go on his way because the words were sealed (Daniel 12:8-9). I know that feeling. Some days you just have to keep baking without seeing the whole recipe! Look at what he's promised, though: "Blessed is he who waits," and "You will rest, and then you will arise to your inheritance" (Daniel 12:12-13). That's why my ovens stay ready, friend. Wait faithfully, keep pointing people to what's good, and trust the One who knows the end.
